title: Frontend: StickyNotes Component
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind StickyNotes Component. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Add note[data-action=add] creates a note at x=20 with sequential data-note ID and controlled textarea. Move right[data-move=ID] nudges x by 10, clamped at 200; data-x reflects position. Delete[data-delete=ID] removes that note. Preserve text during movement. This exercise tests note editing/position state, not pointer physics or persistence.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Store stable note IDs, content, and logical positions.
alternativeApproaches: Add shared-board synchronization with explicit conflict resolution for concurrent text and position edits.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Drag vs edit; pointer cancel; deleting active note.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
